title: Contractive norm-attaining maps to finite cartesian spaces
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] with a real-valued multiplicative nonarchimedean absolute value. A norm on a $k$-vector space means a definite function $N$ with $N(x+y)\le\max(N(x),N(y))$ and $N(cx)=|c|N(x)$. A finite basis $(w_i)$ is orthogonal when $N(\sum_i c_iw_i)=\max_i|c_i|N(w_i)$. Let $U$ be a normed $k$-vector space. Suppose that for every nonzero $u\in U$ there exist a finite-dimensional normed $k$-vector space $(W_u,N_u)$ having an orthogonal basis and a $k$-linear map $f_u:U\to W_u$ satisfying $$N_u(f_u(v))\le N(v)\quad(v\in U),\qquad N_u(f_u(u))=N(u).$$ Then every finite-dimensional $k$-linear subspace $V\subseteq U$, with its restricted norm, has an orthogonal $k$-basis. The zero space and empty basis are included, with empty maximum zero. No completeness, spherical completeness, stability of $k$, or algebra structure on $U$ is assumed.

proof.text: Induct on $n$, with the claim quantified over all subspaces $V\subseteq U$ possessing an algebraic basis of length $n$. For $n=0$, $V=0$ and the empty basis has the required formula. For $n>0$ fix such a basis $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ and set $u=e_1\ne0$. Choose the hypothesized map $f=f_u$ and an orthogonal basis $w_1,\ldots,w_m$ of its target. Write $f(v)=\sum_i c_i(v)w_i$; each $c_i:U\to k$ is linear by uniqueness of basis expansions. Since $N_u(f(u))=N(u)>0$, $m>0$ and some $j$ satisfies $|c_j(u)|N_u(w_j)=N(u)$; in particular $c_j(u)\ne0$.

source.place: Independent coordinate-functional proof of the abstract norming criterion suggested by BGR Proposition 3.8.1/10; archival BGR copy unavailable (WANTED in report). No unverified assertion from BGR is used. Step 1.

proof.text: By [def-weil-field], $c_j(u)$ is invertible. Define $\lambda(v)=c_j(v)/c_j(u)$. It is linear and $\lambda(u)=1$. The coordinate norm formula and contractivity give $$|\lambda(v)|N(u)=|c_j(v)|N_u(w_j)\le N_u(f(v))\le N(v)\qquad(v\in U).$$ The first equality uses multiplicativity of the absolute value and the choice of $j$. Thus this scalar functional controls the component along $u$ with constant exactly one.

source.place: Independent coordinate-functional proof of the abstract norming criterion suggested by BGR Proposition 3.8.1/10; archival BGR copy unavailable (WANTED in report). No unverified assertion from BGR is used. Step 2.

proof.text: Put $H=\{v\in V:\lambda(v)=0\}$. It is a linear subspace by linearity of $\lambda$. Every $v\in V$ has the unique decomposition $v=au+h$, where $a=\lambda(v)$ and $h=v-au\in H$; uniqueness follows by applying $\lambda$. For $a\in k$, $h\in H$, put $z=au+h$. Step 2 gives $N(au)=|\lambda(z)|N(u)\le N(z)$. Also $N(h)=N(z-au)\le\max(N(z),N(-au))\le N(z)$, since $N(-au)=N(au)$. The ultrametric inequality gives the reverse bound, so $$N(au+h)=\max(|a|N(u),N(h)).$$

source.place: Independent coordinate-functional proof of the abstract norming criterion suggested by BGR Proposition 3.8.1/10; archival BGR copy unavailable (WANTED in report). No unverified assertion from BGR is used. Step 3.

proof.text: For $2\le i\le n$ set $h_i=e_i-\lambda(e_i)u\in H$. These $n-1$ vectors form an algebraic basis of $H$: if $h=\sum_i a_i e_i\in H$, then $0=\lambda(h)=a_1+\sum_{i\ge2}a_i\lambda(e_i)$ and hence $h=\sum_{i\ge2}a_i h_i$. If $\sum_{i\ge2}b_i h_i=0$, comparison of the $e_i$ coefficients for $i\ge2$ gives every $b_i=0$. This also proves $H=0$ for $n=1$, when the displayed family is empty.

source.place: Independent coordinate-functional proof of the abstract norming criterion suggested by BGR Proposition 3.8.1/10; archival BGR copy unavailable (WANTED in report). No unverified assertion from BGR is used. Step 4.

proof.text: Apply the induction hypothesis to $H\subseteq U$ and its basis of length $n-1$, obtaining a finite orthogonal basis $q_1,\ldots,q_r$ for its restricted norm. All norming maps remain available on $U$; no assertion about a quotient norm is required. The unique decomposition in Step 3 shows that $(u,q_1,\ldots,q_r)$ is a basis of $V$. For arbitrary coefficients, Step 3 and orthogonality on $H$ give $$N\left(au+\sum_i b_iq_i\right)=\max\left(|a|N(u),\max_i|b_i|N(q_i)\right).$$ Empty maxima are zero, so this includes $H=0$ and completes the induction.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NN-3481219b8 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and the full proof. The delivery has no new nodes and leaves the statement unchanged. The statement (for each nonzero u, contractive norm-attaining maps into finite normed spaces with an orthogonal basis imply that every finite-dimensional subspace has an orthogonal basis) is true as written over any valued field; completeness is not needed. Step 1: the induction claim covers every subspace with a basis of length n. N_u(f u)=N(u)>0 gives a target coordinate j that attains the maximum and has c_j(u)≠0. Step 2: def-weil-field gives exactly the inverse that is needed. lambda=c_j/c_j(u) satisfies |lambda(v)|N(u)=|c_j(v)|N_u(w_j)≤N_u(f v)≤N(v). Step 3: H=ker(lambda) inside V, and N(au+h)=max(|a|N(u),N(h)) holds in both directions, including when the two norms are equal. Step 4: h_i=e_i-lambda(e_i)u span H (the difference is lambda(h)u=0) and are independent by their e_i coefficients; n=1 gives H=0. Step 5: the induction hypothesis applies to H with the restricted norm; the decomposition from Step 3 and orthogonality of the basis of H give the formula. Edge cases checked: V=0, dimension 1, trivial absolute value, several attaining coordinates, incomplete k; the non-cartesian norm |a+b xi| with xi in k-hat minus k admits no norming maps, so it is not a counterexample. The only citer, lem-trf-gauss-spectral-coefficient-cartesian step 3, applies the statement literally with W=k_a. This is not a duplicate of lem-trf-cartesian-subspace or lem-trf-cartesian-subspace-scalar-tower, which assume a finite orthogonal ambient space or a scalar tower. The only citation is a definition, so there is no route or tool_uses issue and no cycle. proof_deps equals the union of the uses, and all four search kinds are recorded. BGR is not in literature/, so the proof is correctly marked proof_origin.by=agent and the report lists BGR as WANTED.
